_comment: How a bank credit is classified. Patterns are case-insensitive substrings of the transaction remarks; first match wins, income_rails before non_income. A credit matching nothing falls through to 'personal' and is EXCLUDED from income. Add a new rail here when a new affiliate network starts paying the bank directly.
_non_income_comment: Real money, but not earnings. Kept separate from 'personal' so the future personal-dashboard can chart owner->mother transfers without re-deriving them, and so they can never be mistaken for income.

_alias_comment: Payer names as the tool you actually recognise. Two jobs: turn a legal entity into a real name, and MERGE a tool that pays from more than one profile so its revenue is not split across two rows. Keys are matched case-insensitively against the payer name from PayPal or the network. Anything not listed falls back to automatic suffix stripping (Inc., LLC, Corp, GmbH, Limited, ООД), which already handles most names — only add an entry when that is not enough.
_alias_evidence: IDENTIFY A PAYER FROM ITS OWN TRANSACTION, NOT FROM A GUESS. PayPal carries the payer email and a free-text note, and the note usually names the brand outright. Pull it with: paypal-txns-pp-cli reporting search-get --start-date <iso> --end-date <iso> --fields all --json, then read payer_info.email_address and transaction_info.transaction_note. On 2026-08-30 a guess (Todor Karlikov's LinkedIn says Book Bolt) merged two unrelated payers; the emails disproved it in one command.

_alias_notes.Fliki: Payer 'Nine Thirty Five LLC' (the ninethirtyfive.llc domain). PayPal transaction note on 2026-02-02 reads 'Fliki affiliate' — the payer naming its own brand. 'fliki' is also one of the owner's tracking links.
_alias_notes.Submagic: Not present in this PayPal account at all — zero payments Jan-Aug 2026. Owner says Submagic settles to a different bank account, which is consistent: its money never enters this pipeline, so there is nothing to exclude.
_alias_notes.Book Bolt: 2026-08-31: 'Дигитал Маркетинг Солутионс 2011 ООД' (payer email on the digitalworks.net domain) resolved to Book Bolt and moved here from unidentified_payers. Evidence is the merchant's own ledger, read by bookbolt-pp-cli: Book Bolt's affiliate portal lists exactly two payouts ever, $182.34 on 06/01/2026 and $105.60 on 08/01/2026, and its payout rail is PayPal. The PayPal transaction for $105.60 was received 2026-08-01T17:30:40Z -- the same day, to the cent. The 2026-08-30 rejection of this merge was right that the two are not the same COMPANY (different email domain) but that never settled which TOOL earned the money; a payer of record differs from a brand routinely. Do not re-split them without new evidence from the Book Bolt ledger itself.

_unidentified_comment: Payers that are NOT tools -- agencies and processors that pay out on behalf of brands. A row matched here moves to Untraced carrying its payer name, amount and route, which is a shorter path to the answer than a bare bank reference. Empty since 2026-08-31, when the one entry resolved to Book Bolt via its own merchant ledger. An empty map here is the goal state, not a bug.
_manual_comment: THE EXIT ROUTE FOR UNTRACED MONEY. When the owner works out where a credit came from - a bank asking about the reference, a payout spotted in a network dashboard - record it here once and it is named forever. This runs before every heuristic pass and outranks all of them (confidence 'confirmed'), so nothing can un-name it. Match is on date + amount, which is unique in a passbook. Copy the date and amount straight off the Untraced row in the dashboard. 'route' is the hops before the bank; 'note' is for your future self, and is not shown in the UI. NOTE ON EXCHANGE RATES: money arriving over Airwallex converts at roughly 90-96 INR/USD in 2026, NOT the ~87 an older note in this repo assumed. PayPal settles the same dollars nearer 89 because it keeps a fat FX margin, so PayPal is the wrong yardstick for judging an Airwallex credit. A rate in the low 90s is normal here and is not evidence against a match. NOTE: the six OpenArt rows that lived here were removed on 2026-08-31 when tolt-pp-cli started reading the dashboard directly. Manual attribution is for money no source can see; once a source CAN see it, leaving a manual row here means two claims on one credit, and this pass wins -- which would make the new source look broken.
